article.title: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is in private beta; its license gives licensees 8 hours to disable a feature or roll back after a safety notice
article.summary: Anthropic's license for the self-hosted Managed Agents server sets 8 hours to disable a feature or roll back after a written risk notice. The New Stack reports it; Anthropic's docs list what the server sends.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Anthropic's [blog post](https://claude.com/resources/articles/self-hosted-claude-managed-agents), dated November 12, 2026, says self-hosted Claude Managed Agents "is now available in private beta" and tells readers to contact their Anthropic account team to request access. The server software is covered by a [license agreement](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/self-hosted-managed-agents-license) whose page lists Nov 12, 2026 under "Effective"; its text says the terms are "effective on the date that Licensee first downloads the Binary". Under section 5.3, if Anthropic notifies the licensee in writing that a feature or version presents a safety, security or misuse risk, the licensee must "disable that feature or roll back that version in each Deployment within 8 hours after the notice".

[The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/self-hosted-claude-managed-agents/) reported the license terms; its page metadata dates the article 2026-11-13 at 21:29 UTC. The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic. The New Stack's page states that its owner, Insight Partners, is an investor in OpenAI and Anthropic. The Herald previously reported on the opening of the [Claude Managed Agents public beta](/article/2026-04/22-anthropic-opens-claude-managed-agents-public-beta-charging-eight-cents-per-hour-to-host-enterprise-agents).

## What the license says

The items below are from the [license text](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/self-hosted-managed-agents-license) and are among its terms, not a complete list.

- **Safety updates (5.2).** The licensee must deploy each Safety Update "within 1 business day after Anthropic delivers it". Section 1.11 defines a Safety Update as an Update that Anthropic identifies in writing as "necessary to address a safety, security, or misuse risk"; section 5.2 words the purpose as addressing "critical agent misuse". The Herald found nothing in the license that explains the two wordings, and the license text does not define "business day" or give a time zone for the 8 hours.
- **Other updates (5.4, 5.5).** The licensee is to use commercially reasonable efforts to deploy an Update not designated as a Safety Update or rollback within 30 days, and must stop using a version Anthropic withdraws within 30 days of the notice, or within the period in 5.2 or 5.3 where one applies.
- **Models (3(c), 5.6).** The licensee may not use the software with a Third-Party Model, "except as the Documentation expressly permits". Section 5.6 says Anthropic may decide, for safety reasons, that some or all of a licensee's customers should reach certain Anthropic models only through Anthropic's hosted service.
- **Usage Signals (5.9).** The software "may send observability signals to ensure performance to Anthropic"; the licensee "will not remove, block, alter, or falsify Usage Signals" or route requests to Anthropic models in a way that hides that they come from the software. Anthropic may use them to measure use and monitor compliance.
- **Other terms.** The license covers compiled Binary Code, which the licensee may not modify or reverse engineer (1.3, 2.1, 3(a), 3(g)). Agent Incidents, defined by thresholds the parties agree in writing, are to be reported within 48 hours after confirmation (5.7). Anthropic's total liability is capped at US$100,000.00 (8.2), and either party may end the agreement for convenience on 90 days' written notice (9.2).

## What The New Stack reports

The New Stack describes the same deadlines: customers have "eight hours to disable the affected feature or roll back the version", and one business day to install a designated safety update. Patrick Moorhead, founder and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, says the eight-hour period is tighter than the time most large enterprises typically allow for production changes, and says: "Self-hosted usually means the customer owns the change window." He adds: "This license flips that." He expects regulated buyers to push back on the rollback deadline and the telemetry terms. Jason Andersen, also an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, calls the terms "a reasonable ask" for enterprises and says the telemetry clause and the safeguards requirement are broadly in line with how cloud vendors would try to prevent misuse.

The Herald compared the outlet's description with the license text. The deadlines match sections 5.2 and 5.3. On models, The New Stack writes that the license bars other developers' models "unless Anthropic expressly permits them"; section 3(c) of the license makes the exception "as the Documentation expressly permits", which names the documentation rather than Anthropic. Anthropic's [inference page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted/inference-provider) states that "Agents name models by their Claude API IDs", and its gateway examples map Claude API model IDs to the gateway's own IDs.

## What Anthropic's product pages say

The [announcement post](https://claude.com/resources/articles/self-hosted-claude-managed-agents) describes where the agents, credentials and session history live and says model requests can go to Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry or a customer's own gateway. The post text the Herald read does not mention the license terms above; that is an omission, not a disagreement.

The docs page on [data and access](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-data-and-access) states that the server "connects to Anthropic only when the Claude API is its inference provider". When it is, each model call carries up to three ID headers, and the page says "No setting turns them off"; the server also checks its credential with the Claude API at startup and every 60 seconds by default, and requests carry a User-Agent header that, the page says, Anthropic can use to count usage. The page does not use the phrase "Usage Signals", and the license does not list which signals it means, so the Herald cannot say whether these items are the signals section 5.9 describes. The two documents are not reconciled here.

The [upgrade page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted/upgrade) says that after a patch upgrade the old release can be deployed again because both releases use the same schema, while after a minor or major upgrade it may be necessary to restore a database backup, and "A restore loses everything that clients wrote after the backup began." Neither the upgrade page nor the license says which of these paths a given 8-hour notice would involve; the upgrade page does not mention the notice period. The docs [overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted) says the customer installs each release itself and names the license.

## What we don't know

- None of the cited sources states how many organisations have access to the private beta or whether the license will change when the beta ends.
- None of the cited sources reports an instance of Anthropic issuing a notice under section 5.3.
- The New Stack is the only outlet independent of Anthropic among the cited sources, and the analysts' views reach the Herald only through it.
